sources.researchNote: The Boston Public Library dates the poster to about 1920–1930. Sébille’s dates, 1874–1953, follow his authority records (BnF 147014081; VIAF 67528549). The poster shows the boat-train connection the French Line ran to its liners at Le Havre, by which Kaper sailed in 1934; it does not show the Champlain.

media.title: Paris–Havre–New York — French Line poster by Albert Sébille, c. 1920–1930
media.description: Colour lithograph poster by the marine painter Albert Sébille, issued jointly by the Chemins de fer de l’État and the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique to advertise the boat train from Paris to the liners at Le Havre. Passengers leave the train on the quay and board the ship under a canopy lettered “French Line”. Printed by Novia, Paris.
media.altText: Poster of a steam locomotive drawing up on a quay beside the black hull and red funnels of an ocean liner, with passengers crossing to the ship, under the words Paris Havre New York.
media.publicCaption: “Paris–Havre–New York”: the French Line boat train at the Le Havre quay, on a poster by Albert Sébille of about 1920–1930.
media.publicCreditLine: Albert Sébille; Chemins de fer de l’État and Compagnie Générale Transatlantique; printed by Novia, Paris. Boston Public Library, Travel Posters; via Digital Commonwealth.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. Albert Sébille died in 1953, so the French term of the author’s life plus seventy years has ended. The poster was published in France before 1931, which puts it out of copyright in the United States by date, whatever the URAA restored. The Boston Public Library offers its digitisation under CC BY-NC-ND; that licence does not restrict the public-domain poster itself.

places.publicNote: Kaper sailed from Le Havre to New York aboard the S.S. Champlain in 1934. The marker is placed at city level. At the time, CGT liners used the port’s earlier transatlantic quays: the Gare Maritime on quai Johannès-Couvert opened in May 1935, with the Normandie, and was destroyed in the 1944 bombing of Le Havre.
